title: US Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Hold 3-Hour Talks With Putin in Moscow as Russia Orders 72-Hour Pause on Kyiv Strikes
detail: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential adviser Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on September 5 and held more than three hours of talks with President Vladimir Putin, followed by dinner, in an effort to revive Ukraine peace negotiations that had been frozen for nearly eight months. Ahead of the visit, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Putin ordered a 72-hour pause on strikes against Kyiv starting at midnight, tying it to preparations for the envoys' trip; Ukraine reciprocated with a matching pause on long-range strikes against Moscow. Trump and Ukrainian officials indicated the envoys carried a renewed ceasefire proposal. No immediate details of the talks' outcome were announced, though Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov later called them 'useful.' Witkoff and Kushner were scheduled to travel to Kyiv the next day to meet Ukrainian officials.

media.caption: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin, September 5, 2026

title: IAEA Brokers Seventh Localized Ceasefire to Repair Power Line to Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant
detail: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi announced a localized ceasefire took effect on September 5 to allow Ukrainian technicians to repair the 330-kilovolt Ferosplavna-1 power line supplying the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, which lost its sole remaining offsite power connection on August 20 due to military activity north of the Dnipro River. The plant had relied on emergency diesel generators to cool its six reactors and spent fuel pools since the outage, with officials warning of a potential station blackout. Under the truce, Ukrainian crews began repairs following demining of the area, monitored by an IAEA team on site — the seventh such IAEA-brokered localized ceasefire at the plant to date.

media.caption: IAEA-brokered ceasefire enables power line repairs at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, September 5, 2026

title: Russia Rejects Truce, Kills 5 in Ballistic Missile Strike on Kamianske Steel Plant
detail: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile strike on the Kametstal steel plant in Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, in the early hours of September 5, killing five plant employees and injuring five others, according to regional Governor Oleksandr Hanzha. Three of the wounded were hospitalized, including a 30-year-old woman in intensive care. Kametstal, which had continued operating throughout the war, halted operations following the strike. The attack came the same day Russia announced a 72-hour pause on strikes against Kyiv to accommodate visiting US envoys, underscoring that the truce did not extend to the rest of the country.

media.caption: Aftermath of the Russian ballistic missile strike on the Kametstal plant in Kamianske, September 5, 2026
